issues.description: Return type mismatch for singFarmSong(): the problem statement (and UML) describe/expect the method to print the song (void) while the template declares public void singFarmSong() and the solution returns a String (public String singFarmSong()). This inconsistency can confuse students about whether to implement a void method that prints to stdout or to return the full song as a String to be asserted in tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the API across problem, template and solution. Either: (A) make singFarmSong() return void everywhere and print the song (update the solution to print and return void), or (B) update the problem statement and template to specify that singFarmSong() returns a String containing the whole song (and adapt the UML to show a String return). Choose one approach and apply it consistently to avoid student confusion.

issues.description: Parameter mismatch for singFarmSongVerse: the UML in the problem statement specifies singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal) but the template's private helper method currently has no Animal parameter (it is commented out), while the solution implements private String singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This discrepancy may lead students to implement the helper incorrectly or be uncertain about the expected signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template helper signature match the UML and the solution by declaring private singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) with the correct parameter. Alternatively, update the UML/problem statement if the helper is intentionally parameterless. Keeping the signature consistent will prevent students from implementing mismatched method signatures.
